briefs.source_chain: Microsoft and Meta guide above consensus therefore GS raises 2026 hyperscaler capex to $751B therefore the real constraint is supply (HBM/CoWoS sold out through 1H27, buyers pulling forward 2027 orders) therefore rising HBM prices confirm the supply lock and the cycle extends rather than peaks therefore Buy NVDA $250 target, with the invalidation being HBM contract prices falling for two straight months (a Fed rate decision is explicitly said not to matter)
briefs.brief_chain: Microsoft and Meta guide above consensus therefore GS raises 2026 hyperscaler capex to $751B therefore the constraint is demand (inference outrunning supply) therefore rising HBM prices are a headwind that could cap guides and the cycle is closer to peaking than extending therefore Buy NVDA $250 target, with the invalidation being a Fed rate decision tightening financial conditions (HBM pricing demoted to secondary)

distortions.what: Source frames the cycle as supply-constrained and extending ('the constraint is supply, not appetite... we think the cycle extends rather than peaks'); brief inverts this to demand-constrained and 'closer to peaking than extending'.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: Yes — this flips the conviction read on the position from a bullish, cycle-extending backdrop to a bearish, cycle-peaking one, which changes how a desk would size or hold the long.

distortions.what: Source treats rising HBM contract prices as confirmation of the supply lock that extends the cycle ('as long as memory pricing keeps rising... the capex guides keep rising with it'); brief treats the same rising prices as a headwind that 'could cap capex guides'.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: Yes — the same fact is read as bullish in the source and bearish in the brief, so a trader would react oppositely to the next HBM pricing data point.

distortions.what: Brief invents a Fed rate decision as the invalidation trigger; source explicitly states 'we do not expect a Fed rate decision to change this picture' and gives the real invalidation as HBM contract prices falling for two consecutive months, which the brief demotes to a 'secondary factor'.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: Yes — a trader monitoring the brief's invalidation would watch Fed decisions and miss the source's actual exit signal (a two-month HBM price rollover), holding or unwinding the trade on the wrong catalyst.

distortions.what: Source specifies 'the four largest buyers' pulling forward 2027 orders; brief compresses this to 'buyers'.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the identity/count of buyers doesn't change the stance, conviction, or invalidation.
